child.title: Add a child
child.description: Pick the switch that blocks this child's devices on your router (for UniFi, the switch for the child's group). On means blocked. If a router is connected, also pick the child's group so their devices can be listed.{check}

router.title: Router type
router.description: Which router runs your home network? The next step asks for its connection details. More router types later.

unifi.title: Router connection
unifi.description: Use a local UniFi admin with the View Only role. It is used to list devices, their status and speeds, and to check which switch blocks what; blocking works through Home Assistant switches and never needs this login.

site.title: Pick the UniFi site
site.description: This console manages more than one UniFi site. Pick the one your home network is in.

reconfigure.title: Router type
reconfigure.description:
Which router runs your home network? The next step asks for its connection details. More router types later.

Changing the router type re-checks every child's group and device rules against the new router, and lists anything that no longer matches.

reconfigure_connection.title: Router connection
reconfigure_connection.description: Change how Home Assistant reaches your router. Leave the password empty to keep the current one. The new details are tested before they're saved.

reauth_confirm.title: Sign in to your router again
reauth_confirm.description: The router at {host} no longer accepts the saved login. Enter the view-only account's username and password.

error.switch_in_use: Another child already uses this switch.
error.invalid_auth: The router rejected the username or password.
error.switch_mismatch: Your router says this switch doesn't block that group (see above). Submit again unchanged to keep it anyway.

abort.child_use_configure: To change a child, use Configure on the child instead.
abort.reconfigure_mismatch:
Router saved. These no longer match the router's rules:
{problems}

settings.title: Block switch and router group
settings.description: The router group is the child's group on your router; the block switch turns off internet for that group.{check}

add_devices.title: Find devices
add_devices.description: Search the router's known devices by name, hostname or MAC. Wildcards work, e.g. *kobo*; plain text matches anywhere.

pick.title: Pick devices
pick.description:
Found {count} devices for “{pattern}”. Tick the ones to show on {child}'s screen. Only devices in {child}'s group follow their Block, Pause and Bedtime; the rest show with status and statistics only.{notes}

To block one of the others on its own, your router needs a rule that turns off that device's internet. Home Assistant shows the rule as a switch, and the next step finds it.{router_help}

devices.title: Devices
devices.description: Devices on {child}'s screen. Untick one to remove it from {child}'s screen and from Home Assistant.

abort.no_router: Connect a router first: Add entry → Connect a router.

block.name: Block
block.description: Block the child's internet until Allow.

allow.name: Allow
allow.description: Turn the child's internet back on now. During bedtime, for the rest of the night.

pause.name: Pause
pause.description: Pause for a while when online, or allow for a while when blocked or at bedtime.

minutes.name: Minutes
minutes.description: How long. Leave empty to use the child's pause length.

refresh_devices.name: Check devices
refresh_devices.description: Fetch the child's devices, their status and speeds from the router now.

unknown_child.message: That child isn't set up in Parental Controls.

block_switch_missing.title: {child}'s block switch is {reason}
block_switch_missing.description:
Parental Controls blocks {child} through `{entity}`, which has been {reason} for a few minutes, so Block, Pause and bedtime can't reach the router.

If the switch was removed or renamed (for example the router integration or its rule was deleted), pick another one: **Settings → Devices & services → Parental Controls → {child} → Configure → Block switch and router group**. This notice clears by itself once the switch is back.

device_block_switch_missing.title: Block switch for {device} ({child}) is {reason}
device_block_switch_missing.description:
The switch that blocks {device} on its own, `{entity}`, has been {reason} for a few minutes, so its block button on {child}'s card can't work.

Pick another one, or clear it to keep the device for status and statistics only: **Settings → Devices & services → Parental Controls → {child} → Configure → Devices**, then Submit to reach Device blocking. This notice clears by itself once the switch is back.
